content:
Yesterday saw two contradictory reports about next year's iPhone 20th anniversary edition, saying that this device will embody Apple's long-term vision of "a single piece of glass."

As for what we should actually expect, there have been contradictory reports before, but yesterday's divergence was the biggest so far...

What we know so far

Apple's former design chief Jony Ive has often mentioned his long-term vision that the iPhone will eventually become "a single piece of glass." It is widely believed that Apple has continued to pursue this vision even after Ive's departure.

Although Apple generally does not celebrate various anniversaries of its products on a grand scale, the mainstream view is that they aim to get as close to this vision as possible around the iPhone's 20th anniversary. This could include embedding Face ID technology under the display and similarly hiding the front camera beneath the screen.

However, we have already seen contradictory reports about what is expected. While some initially believed this device would be a standalone model similar to the iPhone Air and the upcoming iPhone Ultra, more recent reports have indicated that this design will be applied to next year's iPhone Pro models.

In sequential order, it would be the iPhone 19 Pro, but Apple might want to skip this name to commemorate the anniversary, jumping directly to the iPhone 20 naming.

Yesterday's contradictory reports

Yesterday the situation became even more confusing, with analysts pointing out that Apple has abandoned the concept of launching an all-glass iPhone next year.

However, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman immediately refuted this claim.

The more likely reality

The key point is that Apple's vision for the iPhone does not have a single, ultimate goal. Whatever Apple plans for next year, it will only be one step or several steps toward the science-fiction vision of "a single piece of glass."

The question is not whether this goal will be reached next year, but how many steps Apple will take toward the vision. But whether it's one step or several, it certainly will not be the final step in the evolution of the iPhone's design.

In fact, Gurman revealed that Apple has stepped back slightly from the progress it originally hoped to achieve next year.

It's very likely that analysts at Jefferies also heard the same news, but only received it more recently, so they interpreted it as a complete abandonment of the plan.

My own expectation is that next year's design will be a major step forward — equivalent to the leap made when the iPhone X was launched — but there will be more developments in the years to come. For me, the biggest question is whether the 2027 iPhone will have enough breakthroughs to prompt Apple to adopt some kind of special branding, whether it's labelled as a 20th anniversary edition iPhone (which I think is highly unlikely), given another special name, or skipping a generation and calling it the iPhone 20.

What are your expectations? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
